top_categories.workout_context: 14,435ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
123ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Alpen Challenge Lenzerheide, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Alpen Challenge Lenzerheide's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.
At mile 60 of 117, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
14,435ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Alpen Challenge Lenzerheide. Train it until it feels boring.

Road-specific control matters at Alpen Challenge Lenzerheide. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 117 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 117 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Low-cadence force work supports 14,435ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 14,435ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Alpen Challenge Lenzerheide. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Alpen Challenge Lenzerheide’s 117 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Alpen Challenge Lenzerheide includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Alpen Challenge Lenzerheide rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, TT Threshold, and Over Under to prepare you for 117 miles of mixed terrain in Lantsch/Lenz, Graubünden, Switzerland.
